headings.title: SMTO-GML-0052 — The selected Gateway can't handle Gmail for this account

html:
SMTO-GML-0052 — The selected Gateway can't handle Gmail for this account

GUID: cf6f3cda-c374-5044-ae29-918fa97c9ecd
Slug: gmail-private-gateway-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • Gmail accounts saved with an app password are reached through a Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run work on a computer. The Gateway for this task is missing, offline, or too old to do this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that the Gateway this task uses is listed and connected. If not, make sure its computer is switched on and online. SMTO can't reach this mailbox at all without a connected Gateway.
  2. Select Check for updates. If a newer version is offered for that Gateway, update it at a quiet moment, because updating restarts it and stops its running tasks. Older Gateways don't know how to handle Gmail accounts that use an app password.
  3. Before repeating a send or change, open Gmail and check Sent, Drafts and the affected messages to see whether it already happened. If the Gateway lost contact partway through, the earlier action may still have gone through.
  4. Under the message box, open the Execution target menu and make sure that Gateway is selected. Then ask SMTO to test the Gmail connection with the same account. The test confirms the updated Gateway can now reach Gmail without changing any mail.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected and up to date, and the Gmail connection test succeeds.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and its Gateways. Keep using the same Gmail account; don't switch accounts or sign-in methods to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The private Gmail route through the Gateway was unavailable: the Gateway client lacks the Gmail operation (upgrade required), no run identity was bound, or the Gateway reported a configuration or execution failure.

What this means

  • The selected Gateway could not provide the private Gmail operation route. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The selected Gateway could not provide the private Gmail operation route.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • In Settings › Setup › Gateways confirm the target Gateway is paired, connected, and on a release that exposes gmail_imap v1 and email_smtp (email_gateway_capability_unavailable maps to gmail_imap_gateway_upgrade_required). Update and reconnect it, keep the same account_ref, run gmail.test_connection, and reconcile any write marked effect_unknown before repeating it.
  • Update and reconnect the selected paired Gateway to a release supporting gmail_imap v1 and email_smtp. Keep the same selected account and run gmail.test_connection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
